target_customer: Product, growth and data teams at software and digital companies that pay annual subscriptions for product analytics
problem: Teams could not easily connect user actions in apps to retention and growth; the founders first felt this running their own voice texting app, Sonalight.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free tier, priced on event volume and features
product_category: Product analytics and digital optimization platform

founders.name: Spenser Skates
previous_startups: Sonalight (voice to text app, became Amplitude)
founders.background_notes: Won MIT's Battlecode programming competition two years in a row per the YC page.

founders.name: Curtis Liu
previous_startups: Sonalight (voice to text app, became Amplitude)
founders.background_notes: College friend of Skates per secondary sources.

founders.name: Jeffrey Wang
founders.background_notes: Joined around the analytics pivot per YC's account; not on the YC company page.

exit.reason: Direct listing on Nasdaq on September 28, 2021, no new capital raised in the listing

technical_complexity.rationale: Event ingestion and fast behavioral queries across large datasets was nontrivial infrastructure but built from known techniques.

defensibility.rationale: Historical event data and dashboards created lock in, but instrumentation was simple to replicate and many analytics rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google and others offered free or adjacent analytics; Amplitude stayed independent, listed in 2021, and its stock fell sharply from its peak.

market_need_then: The team built analytics because the voice app Sonalight had poor retention and existing tools did not show why; investors backed the analytics pivot and the company relaunched as Amplitude in February 2014.

identity.logo: Wave shaped A mark inside a circle, with a signature blue per a third-party brand guide summary
identity.visual_style: Clean product software look with an official brand site

rebrands.why: Relaunch after pivoting from the voice texting app to mobile analytics

branding.community_and_virality: Company runs a community page, Amplitude Academy, events and an Amp Champs program; no merch or fan accounts confirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in product analytics with an official brand site and community programs, but no evidence of viral or iconic brand assets.

pivots.from: Sonalight, a voice to text messaging app
pivots.why: Sonalight had poor retention and was too early; the internal analytics tool looked more valuable

outcome_analysis: Amplitude's first product, the Sonalight voice app, failed on retention, and the founders turned their internal analytics tool into Amplitude, relaunching in February 2014. It raised a reported 150 million dollar round at a 4 billion dollar pre-money valuation in June 2021 and direct listed in September 2021, then saw its stock fall from the peak with a 2023 WARN notice covering 83 workers.
notes: Earlier rounds conflict across aggregators and are not recorded as rounds: seed or Series A figures (4 to 10 million, 2012 to 2015), Series D of about 80 million in December 2018, and totals from 336 million to 1.6 billion. The 4 billion figure is a pre-money valuation from a June 2021 funding summary, so post_money is left null. Layoff detail rests on a single WARN tracker page. No dated 2014 competitor sources were found, so the list is empty; Mixpanel and Google Analytics are named only in later retrospectives. Founding year 2012 is the YC batch; Amplitude relaunched in 2014. Name origin not found.
